current_plate.title: El gran palacio de Mitla, provincia de Oaxaca (the Great Palace of Mitla)
current_plate.verdict: NOT a photograph - it is a wood engraving (the caption 'de fotografia' means it was engraved FROM a photograph, but the plate itself is an illustration). Region-accurate and explicitly endorsed by the rule (Oaxaca -> Mitla palace). So it is compliant; the 'Oaxaca is a photo' complaint does not apply to the current file. Only shortfall vs the brief: monochrome and a close-up of the palace wall rather than a valley vista. Options below.

sourcing_note: Genuinely COLOUR public-domain views of Oaxaca are scarce (Carl Nebel's 1836 colour series does not include Oaxaca/Mitla). The strongest Oaxaca-specific illustrations are the Sawkins tinted lithographs of the Mitla valley; a colour Velasco Mexican-highland-valley oil is offered as a region-accurate colour fallback (not Oaxaca itself).

candidates.title: A General View of the Architectural Remains at Mitla
candidates.artist: J. G. Sawkins (drawn); lith. by T. Sinclair, Philadelphia
candidates.collection: Via Wikimedia Commons (Smithsonian / Mayer, Observations on Mexican History and Archaeology)
candidates.fit: A true VALLEY VISTA of Oaxaca - the Mitla ruins on the valley floor with a church, orchards and the surrounding sierra behind. A clear upgrade in composition over the current close-up palace plate. Tinted rather than full colour; light foxing.

candidates.title: The Valley of Mexico from the Santa Isabel Mountain Range
candidates.fit: Magnificent COLOUR Mexican-highland-valley oil (ringed by mountains, distant snow volcanoes, a lake) - captures the Oaxaca valley character in the requested Velasco style. Region-accurate colour FALLBACK only: it depicts the Valley of Mexico, not Oaxaca. Note clearly if used.

candidates.title: General market, Oaxaca (city market beside the arcaded portales and church)
candidates.artist: Engraving from 'The Living Races of Mankind' (c. 1900)
candidates.border_or_mount_to_trim: yes (irregular vignette; white cut-out at lower right)
candidates.fit: An actual OAXACA CITY scene - the market under the arcades with church domes and towers behind; satisfies the 'cityscape for a city' guidance. Drawbacks: monochrome, portrait, and an irregular vignetted edge awkward for a rectangular crop.

candidates.title: Ancient fortification near Mitla
candidates.artist: J. G. Sawkins (drawn); lith. by T. Sinclair, Philadelphia
candidates.fit: A rocky Oaxaca hilltop fortification with agaves and cacti; region-accurate and atmospheric, but a rocky-knoll subject rather than a grand vista or cityscape. Backup option.

recommendation: oaxaca/sawkins-mitla-general-view.jpg (Sawkins, General View of Mitla) - the best genuinely Oaxaca vista, a valley panorama that keeps the rule-endorsed Mitla subject while improving composition over the current close-up. If a full-COLOUR image is required, oaxaca/velasco-valley-of-mexico.jpg is the fallback, but must be flagged as Valley of Mexico rather than Oaxaca.
